findings.title: deleteCache throws a plain Error instead of TRPCError
findings.body: When the credential does not exist or does not belong to the caller the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-TRPCError exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (HTTP 500), so an authorization failure is reported as a server fault, gets logged/reported to error tracking as a crash, and the client cannot distinguish it from a real failure. Use `throw new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN", message: ... })` as the other handlers in this router do.

findings.title: Cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation.onSuccess` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`), nothing invalidates the query that produced `cacheUpdatedAt`. In `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` the `onChanged` prop is optional and is not always supplied, and the query is configured with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so after deleting the cache the dropdown keeps showing the old "Last updated" timestamp and the "Delete cached data" entry until a full page reload, making it look like the deletion failed.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is hard-coded to en-US formatting
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` ignores the user's locale and 12h/24h `timeFormat` preference stored on the user, so non-US users see MM/DD/YYYY and AM/PM dates inside an otherwise localized UI (the surrounding string is translated via `cache_last_updated`). Use the user's locale/time-format (e.g. the existing dayjs/`useTimePreferences` helpers) instead of a literal "en-US".

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt
findings.body: The groupBy query selects `MAX(updatedAt)` for the given credentialIds without filtering on `expiresAt >= now()`, while `getCachedAvailability` only serves non-expired rows. As a result the UI will report a credential as having a cache ("Cache Status / Last updated …") and offer "Delete cached data" even when every cached row is expired and no availability request can be served from it, giving users a misleading view of cache health.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt/googleChannelId that are never used
findings.body: `UserWithCalendars` (an exported type consumed outside this file, e.g. by the platform API v2 calendars service and other callers of `getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb`) was widened to require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars`, but neither field is read anywhere in this module. Any caller that selects only `externalId`/`integration`/`eventTypeId` will now fail type-check, and `UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession` had to be changed to fetch two extra columns per selected calendar into the session payload purely to satisfy the type. Revert the type tightening unless the fields are actually needed.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with an empty data object to bump updatedAt
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` relies on Prisma implicitly writing the `@updatedAt` column when `data` is empty. This is implicit/undocumented behaviour — if Prisma emits no SET clause the call is a pure no-op write — and even when it works it issues an extra UPDATE over every SelectedCalendar row of the credential on every cache refresh (including rows that were not refreshed), which runs on the cache cron for every watched credential. The PR description itself notes `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed by the frontend (the UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt`), so this write appears unnecessary; if it is needed, pass an explicit `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId types data as SelectedCalendarUpdateInput
findings.body: `updateMany` accepts `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`, not `SelectedCalendarUpdateInput`. Using the single-record update type lets callers pass nested relation operations (e.g. `{ user: { connect: { id } } }`) which type-check but fail at runtime with a Prisma validation error. Change the parameter type to `Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateManyMutationInput`.

findings.title: Dev script writes .env outside the repository
findings.body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is resolved relative to the current working directory, not to the script location. The documented way of running repo scripts is from the repository root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`), which makes the script create/modify a `.env` file in the parent directory of the checkout (and print "Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL" as if it had succeeded), while the app's real `.env` is left untouched. Resolve the path from `$(dirname "$0")/..` instead.

findings.title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and breaks on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E "s|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` uses the BSD syntax where `-i` takes a separate (empty) suffix argument. With GNU sed (Linux CI/dev containers) the empty string is parsed as the script/first file operand and the command fails with "can't read : No such file or directory", leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` un-updated while the script still reports success. Use `sed -i.bak`/a temp-file approach, or branch on the platform.

findings.title: dev:cron uses npx tsx but tsx is not a dependency
findings.body: `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` invokes a binary that is not declared in `devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is, and it is still used by the `check-changed-files` and `translate-locales` scripts). `npx` will download an unpinned `tsx` from the network on each run (or prompt), which fails in offline/CI environments and is inconsistent with the yarn-workspace setup. Add `tsx` to devDependencies and call it via `yarn tsx`, or leave the script on `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the feature in this PR.

findings.title: Cache status lookup bypasses the calendar-cache feature flag
findings.body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, so the `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` added in this PR is never used and an extra `calendarCache.groupBy` query is executed on every `connectedCalendars` request even for deployments/teams where calendar cache is disabled (and also when `credentialIds` is empty, producing a pointless `IN ()` query). Route through the feature-flag aware factory, or skip the query when there are no credentialIds / the feature is off.

findings.title: Migration comment contradicts the statement and backfill produces misleading timestamps
findings.body: The generated warning block says the required column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement does supply `DEFAULT NOW()`; the stale comment will mislead reviewers/operators about the migration's safety. In addition, all pre-existing rows are backfilled with the migration time, so immediately after deploy the new UI will report long-stale caches as "Last updated: <deploy time>". Consider removing/correcting the comment and documenting (or backfilling from `expiresAt - CACHING_TIME`) the known inaccuracy.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache authorization or cache-status query
findings.body: `deleteCacheHandler` performs an ownership check that gates a destructive `calendarCache.deleteMany`, and `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` is new behaviour surfaced in the UI, yet neither has a unit test. A regression in the `userId` predicate would let a user delete another user's calendar cache, and nothing would catch it. Add tests covering: deletion for an owned credential, rejection for a credential owned by another user, and the credential→updatedAt mapping returned by the repository.
